children: was bullish in the third quarter of 2026, with several high-profile investors strengthening or maintaining their positions in the chipmaker, while a couple of funds decreased their exposure.
Among the biggest buyers, Tiger Global boosted its Nvidia holdings to 12M shares from 11.2M shares. Altimeter increased its Nvidia holdings from 9.41M shares to 10.01M shares.
Additionally, Senator Investment Group also strengthened its stake to 444K shares from 337K shares.
Separately, Third Point initiated a new position in Nvidia
, adding 1.5M shares, while Corvex Management maintained its holding of 16K Nvidia shares.
On the other hand, Soros Capital and Soros Fund cut their exposure to the semiconductor giant.
Soros Capital reduced its NVDA holding from 77K shares to 10K shares, while Soros Fund cut its holding to 859K shares from 1.06M shares.

For the period ending Oct. 25, Nvidia said it earned an adjusted $2.68 per share as revenue soared 103% year-over-year to $115.84B. Data center revenue flew past expectations, coming in at $107.6B, compared to estimates of $101.87B.
However, the company's shares have slipped more than 32% since the start of the fourth quarter, mainly due to Nvidia's
top boss Jensen Huang's abrupt departure following his admission of infidelity, including an alleged relationship with a woman whom U.S. intelligence officials reportedly identified as a Chinese spy.
